artworks.title: KERNELKEVIN
artworks.text: BE THE KEVIN YOU WANT TO SEE
artworks.descriptionHtml:
High Resolution Version (click to expand)

Kernel Kevin is presented as both figure and principle: a portrait composed entirely of corn kernels, arranged into a face that is immediately familiar and quietly unsettling. The image appears at first to be a playful mosaic, but the longer one looks, the more it suggests intention—ritual, even—behind its construction. Each kernel functions as both material and message.

The card frames Kevin not as an individual, but as a recursive idea. He is the kernel and the colonel, the seed and the authority, the origin and the echo. The accompanying text reinforces this loop, insisting that Kevin is not something to be discovered but something already inhabited. Identity collapses inward. Distinctions dissolve. You are Kevin, and Kevin has always been you.

Visually, the work borrows from the language of collectible fantasy cards: parchment textures, ornamental borders, symbolic insignia. These familiar tropes lend the piece a false sense of order, which only heightens the absurdity of its subject. The rarity score—set pointedly at zero—undercuts the entire economy of value such cards normally uphold, suggesting that what is universal cannot be rare.

An archival note at the bottom introduces a second layer of fiction. The image is described as a reconstruction of a lost corn-kernel collage, once held in quiet reverence somewhere in the Yucatán Peninsula. The original artwork is said to have disappeared, surviving only through a reported vision recounted by an unnamed witness. Whether this history is sincere, fabricated, or misremembered is deliberately unclear. The tone mimics academic restraint while quietly admitting that none of this can be verified.

Kernel Kevin ultimately operates as a parody of myth-making itself: how symbols are born, how authority is assigned, how meaning accretes around objects that may have begun as jokes, accidents, or idle arrangements of grain. It invites the viewer to laugh, then asks—without answering—why so many belief systems are built the same way.

In the end, Kevin does not demand belief. He merely insists on recognition.

artworks.title: ISITPEPE
artworks.text:
This token is dedicated to dark ink studios.

Legend is he had a fake common REJECTED by one of the jamies for not being pepe enough, with the response..

ISITPEPE?


that my friends is illgeal. ALL PEPES ARE FAKE COMMONS. Read your own website lads :) xx

This asset then mysteriously dissapeared.
artworks.descriptionHtml:
The tale of ISITPEPE begins, as all true folklore does, in dark ink. Not the ink of permanence, but the ink that runs, that stains, that refuses to fix meaning. Within Counterparty’s shadowed chronicles it is remembered as homage to the impossible: the only ever rejected Fake common, offered by Dark Ink himself. To be dismissed as too Fake, or perhaps not PEPE enough, is to tear open the very category of fakery. How can a KEVIN be refused for being Fake? What lies beneath that paradox?

 

And here the voices of the elders intrude. Scrilla, lord and master of the Fake Rare, once decreed that the Kevins were outlaw — fools and idiots, cast beyond the pale. A judgment thought to be the hidden prerogative of the inner Pepe collective. Yet in time it became clear: this was more divine verdict than ironic accolade, a title previously reserved for the exalted arbitragers of imaginary trading cards themselves. For what else is more fitting in a kingdom where all value is a masquerade?

 

But ISITPEPE is not only parody or jest. It is the mirror held up to our condition. A reminder that in this realm, everything is Fake. The grass beneath us, the stories handed down to us, the idols we exalt, even the histories we swear by. Peel back one mask, and you do not find reality, only another mask, another performance, another counterfeit. Look behind the Fake, and still it is Fake. Look behind that again — Fake. The spiral has no anchor.

The card exists in a sacred supply of 33. Not by chance, but as a gesture toward degrees of so-called enlightenment — steps that might lead upward, or inward, or nowhere at all. For what is enlightenment, if there is no one here to be enlightened? What is the path, if the climber himself is an apparition? Perhaps the thirty-third degree is not achievement, but the revelation that there was nothing to achieve.

Is it Pepe? Is it Kevin? Is it Fake? Or are they all the same?

In Lak’ech.
